newsitem.title: USA: Fire still burning at Excel's Ottuma, Iowa plant.
newsitem.headline: Fire still burning at Excel's Ottuma, Iowa plant.

text.p: Fire fighters continued to battle flames at Excel Corp's Ottumwa, Iowa, hog slaughtering and pork plant and a fire department official said flames broke out in a new area Tuesday morning.
"They (flames) are not under control yet," said Assistant Chief Ken Jordan of the Ottumwa Fire Department. "It is going to take another 24 hours."
Fire fighters have been battling the fire since late Sunday, and the plant remains closed Tuesday after being closed Monday.
Excel, based in Wichita, Kan., is owned by Cargill Inc.
Jordan said about 10 additional fire fighters were called in this morning from surrounding communities to battle the blaze, which was confined to the roof area.
Jordan said by Tuesday morning the fire broke through the roof in another area of the plant, but he did not say which area. The fire initially was confined to the plant's loading facility.

Mark Klein, Excel Corp spokesman, said it is not known when the plant, which can slaughter 9,600 hogs a day, will reopen. He said hogs normally destined for the Ottumwa plant have been diverted to Excel plants in Beardstown, Ill., and Marshall, Mo.
The concrete-block plant was built in 1976 and purchased by Excel in 1987 from Hormel Foods Corp, said Klein.
Construction is under way at the plant which will add storage space and increase the slaughter capacity to about 15,000 head a day, said Klein.
The construction is in an area away from the fire.
The cause of the fire was still under investigation, sources said.
